title: The Voynich Manuscript Mystery
hook: In 1912 a Polish book dealer acquired a strange codex in Italy that defied all translation.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: In 1912, Wilfrid Voynich bought a mysterious codex in Italy that no one could read.

shots.caption: V O Y N I C H PAGE

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: It holds 240 vellum pages of unknown script and vivid botanical drawings.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Radiocarbon dating in 2009 dated the vellum to around 1420, early 15th century.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: Handwriting study finds the script matches no known alphabet, and ink contains iron gall.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: One theory claims the codex is a medieval hoax meant to impress patrons.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: AI analysis in 2023 spotted language-like patterns, yet translation remains impossible.

end.line: What do you think the Voynich code really says?

description: Explore the baffling Voynich Manuscript and the clues that still perplex researchers.

facts.claim: Wilfrid Voynich bought the codex in 1912 in Italy.
The manuscript contains about 240 vellum pages with unknown script and botanical illustrations.
Radiocarbon dating in 2009 placed the vellum's origin to around 1420 (early 15th century).
facts.source: Nature, 2009 - Radiocarbon dating of the Voynich manuscript

facts.claim: Handwriting analysis shows the script matches no known alphabet.
facts.source: University of Arizona, 2015 - Voynich script analysis

facts.claim: AI analysis in 2023 identified language-like statistical patterns but no translation.
facts.source: MIT Technology Review, 2023 - AI study of Voynich manuscript
